name: Smoke test
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Convert JSON to TypeScript (step output)
        id: ts
        uses: ./
        with:
          json: '{"id": 42, "email": "ada@example.com"}'
          mode: ts
          root: User

      - name: Assert TS output non-empty + correct shape
        env:
          CODE: ${{ steps.ts.outputs.code }}
        run: |
          echo "$CODE"
          [ -n "$CODE" ] || { echo 'empty TS output'; exit 1; }
          echo "$CODE" | grep -q 'interface User' || { echo 'expected `interface User`'; exit 1; }

      - name: Convert to TS type alias
        id: ts_type
        uses: ./
        with:
          json: '{"id": 42}'
          mode: ts
          type: 'true'
          root: User

      - name: Assert type alias output
        env:
          CODE: ${{ steps.ts_type.outputs.code }}
        run: |
          echo "$CODE"
          echo "$CODE" | grep -q 'type User' || { echo 'expected `type User`'; exit 1; }

      - name: Convert to Zod (write to output-path)
        uses: ./
        with:
          json: '{"id": 42, "email": "ada@example.com"}'
          mode: zod
          root: User
          output-path: out/user.zod.ts

      - name: Assert Zod file written
        run: |
          test -s out/user.zod.ts
          cat out/user.zod.ts
          grep -q 'z.object' out/user.zod.ts

      - name: Convert to Valibot
        uses: ./
        with:
          json: '{"id": 42, "email": "ada@example.com"}'
          mode: valibot
          root: User
          output-path: out/user.valibot.ts

      - name: Assert Valibot file written
        run: |
          test -s out/user.valibot.ts
          cat out/user.valibot.ts
          grep -q 'v.object' out/user.valibot.ts

name: 'JSON to TypeScript, Zod, or Valibot'
description: 'Convert a JSON sample into a TypeScript interface, Zod schema, or Valibot schema. Composite action, no Node setup, ~1s cold start.'
author: 'SolvoHQ'
branding:
  icon: 'code'
  color: 'blue'
inputs:
  json:
    description: 'JSON sample to convert (string).'
    required: true
  mode:
    description: 'Output target. One of: ts | zod | valibot.'
    required: false
    default: 'ts'
  root:
    description: 'Name of the root interface / type alias / schema in the output.'
    required: false
    default: 'Root'
  type:
    description: 'TS mode only — when true, emit a `type` alias instead of an `interface`.'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  output-path:
    description: 'Path inside the workspace to write the generated code to. If unset, the code is exposed as the `code` step output instead.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  api-url:
    description: 'Override the API endpoint.'
    required: false
    default: 'https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/convert'
outputs:
  code:
    description: 'Generated code. Populated only when output-path is unset.'
    value: ${{ steps.convert.outputs.code }}
runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - id: convert
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_JSON: ${{ inputs.json }}
        INPUT_MODE: ${{ inputs.mode }}
        INPUT_ROOT: ${{ inputs.root }}
        INPUT_TYPE: ${{ inputs.type }}
        INPUT_OUTPUT_PATH: ${{ inputs.output-path }}
        INPUT_API_URL: ${{ inputs.api-url }}
      run: ${{ github.action_path }}/run.sh

# JSON → TypeScript / Zod / Valibot — GitHub Action

Convert a JSON sample into a **TypeScript interface**, **Zod schema**, or **Valibot schema** inside any GitHub Actions workflow. Either capture the result as a step output, or write it straight into your repo so a later step can commit the regenerated types.

This action is a thin wrapper around the public [json-to-ts](https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/) HTTP API. Same algorithm as the hosted converter — three artifacts (UI, HTTP API, this Action), one parity contract.

[![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-live-brightgreen.svg)](https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/)
[![HTTP API](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTTP%20API-/api/convert-78dce8.svg)](https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## Quickstart

```yaml
- uses: SolvoHQ/json-to-ts-action@v1
  id: types
  with:
    json: '{"id": 42, "email": "ada@example.com"}'
    mode: ts                       # ts | zod | valibot
    root: User                     # name of the generated type / schema
    output-path: src/types/user.ts # optional — write to a file
```

## Inputs

| name          | required | default                                          | description |
|---------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `json`        | yes      | —                                                | JSON sample to convert (string). |
| `mode`        | no       | `ts`                                             | One of `ts`, `zod`, `valibot`. |
| `root`        | no       | `Root`                                           | Name of the root type / schema. |
| `type`        | no       | `false`                                          | `ts` mode only — emit `type` alias instead of `interface`. |
| `output-path` | no       | (unset)                                          | If set, the generated code is written to this path inside the workspace. If unset, it is exposed as the `code` step output. |
| `api-url`     | no       | `https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/convert` | Override the API endpoint. |

## Outputs

| name   | description |
|--------|-------------|
| `code` | Generated code. Populated only when `output-path` is unset. |

## Usage examples

### 1. TypeScript interface, written to a file

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4

- uses: SolvoHQ/json-to-ts-action@v1
  with:
    json: ${{ steps.fetch_sample.outputs.body }}
    mode: ts
    root: ApiResponse
    output-path: src/generated/api-response.ts
```

### 2. Zod schema, captured as a step output

```yaml
- uses: SolvoHQ/json-to-ts-action@v1
  id: schema
  with:
    json: '{"event":"checkout.session.completed","data":{"object":{"id":"cs_test_123"}}}'
    mode: zod
    root: StripeEvent

- name: Print the generated schema
  run: echo "${{ steps.schema.outputs.code }}"
```

### 3. Valibot schema, regenerated and committed back to the repo

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4

- uses: SolvoHQ/json-to-ts-action@v1
  with:
    json: ${{ secrets.SAMPLE_PAYLOAD }}
    mode: valibot
    root: WebhookPayload
    output-path: src/schemas/webhook.valibot.ts

- run: |
    git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
    git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
    git add src/schemas/webhook.valibot.ts
    git diff --cached --quiet || (
      git commit -m 'chore: regenerate webhook schema'
      git push
    )
```

## How it works

This is a **composite (bash) action**. It does one thing:

1. POSTs your `json` input to `https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/convert`.
2. Either writes the response to `output-path`, or exposes it as the `code` step output.

No Node setup, no Docker image, no bundled emitter — just `curl` and `jq`, both preinstalled on every GitHub-hosted runner. Cold start ≈ 1 second.

If the API is unreachable or returns a non-200, the step fails loudly with a `::error::` annotation. Empty output is also treated as an error.

### Why curl-the-API instead of bundling the emitter?

So upgrades to the converter (new JSON shapes, smarter unions, edge-case fixes) flow into your CI workflow automatically — no `@v2` bump needed. The hosted [json-to-ts API](https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/) is the single source of truth for the conversion algorithm. The hosted UI, the npm CLI, and this Action are three parity-checked clients of one emitter.

## See also

- **Hosted UI** — paste JSON, get TS / Zod / Valibot, copy out: <https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/>
- **HTTP API docs** — <https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/>
- **Source repo (monorepo)** — [SolvoHQ/json-to-ts](https://github.com/SolvoHQ/json-to-ts)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# json-to-ts-action runner.
# Posts the user's JSON sample to the json-to-ts /api/convert endpoint and
# either writes the response to output-path or exposes it as a step output.
# Inputs come in via INPUT_* env vars set by action.yml (composite action
# convention) — never via positional args, so command-injection from a
# JSON sample with quotes/newlines is impossible.

api="${INPUT_API_URL:-https://json-to-ts-app.netlify.app/api/convert}"
mode="${INPUT_MODE:-ts}"
root="${INPUT_ROOT:-Root}"
type_flag="${INPUT_TYPE:-false}"
output_path="${INPUT_OUTPUT_PATH:-}"
json_input="${INPUT_JSON:-}"

if [[ -z "$json_input" ]]; then
  echo "::error::input 'json' is required" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "$mode" in
  ts|zod|valibot|typescript|interface|type) ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::invalid mode '$mode' (expected: ts | zod | valibot)" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

case "$type_flag" in
  true|false) ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::invalid type '$type_flag' (expected: true | false)" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Build the request body with jq so quotes / newlines in the JSON sample
# are encoded correctly. --argjson type ensures it's a real boolean.
body=$(jq -n \
  --arg j "$json_input" \
  --arg m "$mode" \
  --arg r "$root" \
  --argjson t "$type_flag" \
  '{json: $j, mode: $m, root: $r, type: $t}')

resp_file=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$resp_file"' EXIT

http_code=$(curl -sS -X POST "$api" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary "$body" \
  -o "$resp_file" \
  -w '%{http_code}' \
  --max-time 30 \
  --retry 2 --retry-delay 1) || {
    echo "::error::curl failed reaching $api (network error or timeout)" >&2
    exit 1
}

if [[ "$http_code" != "200" ]]; then
  err=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$resp_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  echo "::error::API returned HTTP $http_code: ${err:-(no error message)}" >&2
  cat "$resp_file" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

code=$(jq -r '.output // empty' "$resp_file")
if [[ -z "$code" ]]; then
  echo "::error::API returned empty output" >&2
  cat "$resp_file" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -n "$output_path" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$output_path")"
  printf '%s' "$code" > "$output_path"
  bytes=$(wc -c < "$output_path")
  echo "wrote $bytes bytes to $output_path"
else
  # Multi-line $GITHUB_OUTPUT delimiter idiom.
  delim="EOF_${RANDOM}_${RANDOM}_${RANDOM}_$$"
  {
    printf 'code<<%s\n' "$delim"
    printf '%s\n' "$code"
    printf '%s\n' "$delim"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  bytes=$(printf '%s' "$code" | wc -c)
  echo "set step output 'code' ($bytes bytes)"
fi
